It's been nearly seven years since developer House House released its breakthrough title, Untitled Goose Game. The company's follow-up, a co-op puzzle-solving game called Big Walk, is out now, and it's already achieved an unexpected critical milestone on PlayStation Plus Essential.

title: Big Walk Just Hit A Major Milestone On PS Plus

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
The blockbuster buyout of Electronic Arts has been completed, with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund taking ownership of the gaming giant in the biggest leveraged buyout (LBO) in the history of commerce.

The $55 billion deal includes billions in debt for EA, which has prompted fears of massive cost-cutting with projected layoffs, studio closures, and game cancellations. Nothing has been confirmed as of yet, however.

"This moment recognizes the extraordinary people whose creativity, ambition, and passion have made EA one of the world's leading interactive entertainment companies," said EA CEO Andrew Wilson in the
title: EA Has Officially Been Sold, And What Comes Next Could Be Painful

description:
In recent years, the trading card game (TCG) environment has seen a boom of new games entering the market. There are still genre mainstays, like Magic: The Gathering, Pokemon, and Yu-Gi-Oh!, which continue to receive support and feature a thriving secondhand market. However, new original IP TCGs like Flesh and Blood and Sorcery are making rounds at the local game store level and beyond.

But licensed IP TCGs, like One Piece and the upcoming Cyberpunk TCG, have also taken the tabletop world by storm. Riftbound, the League of Legends trading card game, is no exception. After releasing late last year (at lea
title: Riftbound Directors Says Game Used To Be A Lot Like Magic: The Gathering–Until Players Rejected It

author: Levi Winslow
description:
Mistfall Hunter is a fascinating mix of games.

On the one hand, it’s a dark fantasy action-RPG with some deep class-building and light souls-like mechanics. On the other, it’s a PvEvP third-person battle royale that sits firmly in the extraction shooter genre. Typically, I’d avoid the latter kind of game, as my low vision makes shooters difficult for me to play, but for some reason, I just can’t get enough of developer Bellring Games’ take on the extraction shooter. In fact, Mistfall Hunter is changing my mind on the genre as a whole.

Mistfall Hunter is taking the internet by storm, with a concurrent player count surpassing 40,000 on Steam after its July 29 launch. Its formula is familiar to anyone with any experience in the extraction genre. You drop into a world, ki
title: Mistfall Hunter Has Made Me A Believer In Extraction Games

author: Myles Obenza
description:
During last week's Gen Con, Riftbound, the League of Legends trading card game (TCG), boasted a massive presence. Fans were able to enter two different booths to get their hands on cards and exclusive merchandise, as well as meet some of the talent behind the game's creation and design.

GameSpot was onsite for the show, and had the opportunity to interview Riftbound Game Director Dave Guskin, during which we learned that the team behind the popular TCG is significantly smaller that you might think. At the end of our time with Guskin, the longtime designer reflected on how the game isn't even a year old yet (referring to its English release in October of last year), saying, "It's been so wonderful to have the community grow around the game, and see what people love. I always say, our team is quite small compared to the player base. So we rely on that partnership between development and community to figure out what's awe
title: Turns Out, The Team Behind Riftbound Is Shockingly Small

description:
After launching in English late last year, Riftbound, Riot Games' League of Legends trading card game (TCG), has quickly grown into one of the most popular TCGs to date. The game had a big presence at this year's Gen Con, featuring not one but two large booths that fans could stop by to learn to play, meet some of their favorite creators, and buy convention-exclusive merch.

During the show, GameSpot had the opportunity to sit down with Riftbound game director Dave Guskin to chat about some of the game's history and where we go from here. Talking about League of Legend's massive roster, GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell was curious is if adding new Legends to Riftbound was an intimidating task when pulling from the source material's over 170-characters.

The 2024 Borderlands movie had a cast full of big names, including multiple Oscar winners, and was based on a popular franchise with countless fans. But the film was a critical and commercial disaster. So what happened?

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
With the release date of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave steadily drawing closer, Nintendo has started to reveal more details about the next chapter in its longrunning tactical-RPG series. Ever since Fire Emblem: Awakening successfully brought the series back from the brink of cancellation, the series has gone from strength to strength over the years, evolving its signature gameplay in well-received successor titles like Conquest, Revelations, and Three Houses.

While 2023's Fire Emblem: Engage may not have reached those same heights, Fortune's Weave looks like it's aiming to return to the standard set by Three Houses with the return of Sothis, Crests, and other familiar gameplay mechanics. Today's Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Nintendo Direct had plenty of new details to reveal about the game, and in case you missed it, we've gathered them all up below to show you how the game is shaping up ahead of its September 17 launch
title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave – Everything We Just Learned From The Direct

author: Jason Fanelli
description:
Back at MagicCon: Amsterdam, the Secret Lair team revealed another first for the program: A preconstructed deck themed around a Universes Beyond partnership, with Hatsune Miku taking center stage. Today, on the official DailyMTG news site, Wizards of the Coast has revealed the full 100-card list for the Miku deck--as well as a trial run on a new method for how to purchase the deck for yourself.

The 100-card Hatsune Miku deck is a green/white deck starring Miku as Trostani, Selesnya's Voice, a legendary creature that can both copy tokens and quickly gain life thanks to its activated Populate ability. The deck itself uses token creation, +1/+1 counters, and finishers like Finale of Devastation and Halo Fountain to win the game on the spot.
title: You’ll Have 24 Hours To Buy The Magic: The Gathering Hatsune Miku Commander Deck Next Week, Here’s What In It

description:
Big Walk is one of the best games of 2026. I explain why in my Big Walk review, but if you're reading this, you don't seem to need me to convince you to play it; you're already considering it. Big Walk is an open-world co-op puzzle-adventure with few rules and no quest markers, and part of the fun is in getting lost and exploring the world. I definitely don't want to rob you of that experience.

However, since beating the game, I've heard from others who are getting stumped by some aspects of House House's latest project. So I've put together some Big Walk tips meant to iron out some of the details the game doesn't clearly tell you.

description:
On your journey through Big Walk, one of the puzzles that is likely to stump you--and all but guaranteed to stump you if you find it early--is the 4166, 1899 puzzle. You'll spot a box with a puzzle MacGuffin inside of it, and nothing else but a plank with these numbers on it. So what the heck do you do next? Here's how to solve this one.

How to do the 4166, 1899 puzzle in Big Walk

First, what you need to know is that these are coordinates, if you didn't already surmise that. But coordinates don't help much without a way to read them. For that, I strongly suggest you first complete the red tower. Some exploration spoilers follow from here.

If you're walking and talking with friends in the land of Big Walk, by now you've likely already customized your characters using the paint studio not far from where the game begins. But did you know there's a second, secret paint studio you'll need to find if you want to access a few special color options and unlock the Big Makeover Achievement or Trophy? Here's what you need to know about how to get shiny in Big Walk.

First, you should know that getting shiny isn't required to beat the game. In fact, my group unlocked the true 100% ending before we got shiny. It's totally optional, unless you really want to also 100% the Achievement or Trophy list. Sorry, Switch players. This one doesn't apply to you the same.

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Beast of Reincarnation is the new action-RPG from Pokemon developer Game Freak, and offers a very different experience from the creature-collecting bliss you're used to. It has three difficulty options, with each being designed so that a wider variety of players can enjoy it, unlike a typical Soulslike game.

Story Mode is best for those who want to play through the narrative without finding combat too challenging. Parry timing is more forgiving, and enemies deal less damage. You'll still need to engage with the combat, but you'll be punished far less for any mistakes you make. If you're playing this for the Game Freak name rather than a passion for a challenging RPG, opt for Story Mode.

Normal Mode is the intended experience, with balanced challenges and normal parry timing. It's intended to encourage you to learn enemy attack patterns, rely on Koo
title: Beast Of Reincarnation Difficulty Options – How To Change Difficulty

description: Game Freak’s foray into the action-RPG genre lands with mixed results.
title: Beast of Reincarnation Review

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
It can be pretty daunting stepping foot into a challenging RPG. Beast of Reincarnation is deliberately intended to make you approach it like a Soulslike, so there's no shame in admitting you need some help from time to time. Thanks to Emma and Koo's well-populated skill trees and synergies, there are plenty of approaches you can take, and what may seem like a tall order can be made a little simpler by taking your time, reading the in-game tutorials, and optimizing your build.

With that in mind, we've put together some essential tips for the early game in Beast of Reincarnation, so that you can progress through the story with a little less friction. But not none at all, because that wouldn't be any fun.
title: Beast Of Reincarnation Tips And Beginner’s Guide

author: Jake Dekker
description:
When you start a new game in Game Freak’s Beast of Reincarnation, a prompt asks if you’d like to play in cinematic mode. This locks the cutscene frame rate to 24 frames per second, but, understandably, leaves the gameplay as is. When I first saw this during my 90-minute preview session last month, it felt like a bold statement from Game Freak. Pokemon, Game Freak’s multigenerational smash-hit, can be described as many things, but cinematic it certainly is not. Unfortunately, aside from its flashy combat and a few cutscenes, Beast of Reincarnation isn't really cinematic, either. Flat performances and robotic animations undermine its fascinating story, bland environments sour its beautiful art direction, and an overall lack of polish hampers its intense combat. Though there are aspects of Beast of Reincarnation that I adored, for each one of them there’s always something that holds it back.

Beast of Reincarnation takes p
title: Beast Of Reincarnation’s Cinematic Focus Fails Its Flashy Action

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Throughout Beast of Reincarnation, you'll unlock plenty of skills for Emma and Koo, but in the early game that can be a little overwhelming. You'll first need to decide where to invest your attribute points, as some skills and mods are locked until you upgrade the main skill they're nested beneath.

While there are several viable approaches, we think the best way to approach the early game while you're getting to grips with the mechanics is to focus on increasing Emma's AoE damage while leaning on Koo's support abilities.
